rationale: Receipt 023f240cad604dd7874ba0054537bc81 (exit 0) completes all six comparisons and they hold: twelve node observations across the two caught-up runs converged in 0-20ms, and the added run_3_immediate case - the demotion issued as soon as the bootstrapped node reported Leader, the construction closest to the harness whose setup event twice reported a stale self view - also converged in 0-20ms with every node's LastIndex ending at the configuration index and no index_passed_while_stale case. The baseline events show why that variant is not actually behind: with the leader campaigning only after about ten to twenty seconds, the followers already had the configuration and the no-op (LastIndex 2) by the time the leader was observed, so the immediate and caught-up constructions coincide in practice. The suspicion recorded in this question is therefore refuted across both constructions, and the isolated field in the extended-window harness (near_node_self_voter true while the leader's configuration reports the demotion) stays unexplained but does not touch the VerifyLeader finding: quorumSize and verifyLeader read the leader's own configuration, which is unambiguous and corroborated by both far nodes, and the only peer that could have answered inside that partition is the reachable node, exactly as the pre-window control that disconnects it shows. I am recording this as the question's current account and leaving that field documented rather than chased further, because no construction I can build reproduces it while every sampled construction shows the entry arriving immediately.

interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts run the same fixed experiment family from identical inputs (cluster construction, per-node timing, DemoteVoter call, 20ms sampling and measured fields); the newer one adds the immediate-demotion case and the waited_baseline field, so the indices for the caught-up runs carry the same measurements in both.
interpretations.rationale: Predicates: every node converges within ten seconds, and no node's view is old while its own log already holds the configuration entry. All six hold, over twelve node observations in this receipt and the same measurements in the previous one, including the immediate-demotion case (near: converged 20ms, last_index_end 3, stale samples only at LastIndex 2 while the configuration index is 3). The source path is unchanged from the earlier account: a peer's own view is the atomic copy written by setLatestConfiguration from processConfigurationLogEntry while appending new entries, or from installSnapshot, so a lag would require the entry not to arrive; no sample shows a node whose log had the entry while its view was still old, and no sample shows a node lagging at all. The question's suspicion is therefore defeated for the constructions tested: a committed voter-to-non-voter transition is reflected by every peer within about one sample interval. The one observation that motivated the question - near_node_self_voter true in the setup events of the two extended-window executions - is retained as an unexplained artefact of that harness's field: it is not reproduced by any construction with per-node sampling, and it cannot explain the VerifyLeader result either way, because that result is decided by the leader's own configuration (voters 3, nonvoters 1, quorum 2) and by the acknowledgements the leader can obtain, with the far voters unreachable.
limitations: Healthy, unloaded, fully connected in-memory cluster in one process; no contention, snapshot install, restart or partition was combined with the transition, so lags under those conditions remain untested rather than excluded.

Seven runs of the discriminating family across both receipts (three plus four), each sampling every 20ms for ten seconds; a rarer stall would need many more repetitions to bound, and a sub-20ms lag is invisible to this sampling.

The immediate-demotion variant turned out not to differ materially because the bootstrapped leader campaigns only after ten to twenty seconds, by which time the followers are already caught up; a construction where the transition truly precedes the followers' adoption was not achieved.
The configuration index used for the consistency check is the leader's LastIndex after the change returns, not an inspection of each follower's log store.
